page.running_head: Animal. in dulcib. aquis Ordo I.

main_text.p: ITAL. Tenca. HISPANICE Tinca. GALLICE Tenche.

GERMANICE Schley, quasi myxon uel muco, uel (ut erudito cuidã placet) limaria. Tincæ quidē ut in limosis sordidisq; locis degunt, ita muco obducuntur, & sese mutuò lambunt. Alij scribunt Schleihe/ nostri Schlig, (g. ita proferentes, ut i. consonam:) alij Siye/ Schleyn. alicubi etiam Gallico vocabulo Tinch appellant. Geldri Lauwen/ Louwen/ Seeld/ Zeeld. Frisij, ni fallor, Oudthund/ (nescio qua ratione:) & alio nomine medicum omnium piscium, (Luciun quidem Tincæ affrictu sua vulnera conglutinare aiūt,) & sutorem nigrum. page.notes: The woodcut shows a tench (Tinca). The text at the foot of the page is set in a mix of roman and italic type; the bottom line is partly cut off by the page edge, and the word "Graunnacker" is printed as shown. Several German and Dutch words are set in black letter and were transcribed as printed; their exact letters are uncertain where marked by the italic and black-letter forms. The "c" below the text is a signature mark.
